$comment: Hard npm-tarball budgets. Required public docs, editor/CEM data, declarations and runtime remain shipped. Re-measured at the 16.0.0 release commit (the release-time CHANGELOG section included): 8,086,877 packed, 32,937,740 unpacked, 3,513 files. Packed size is now 3.3% ABOVE the fixed pre-8.0.0 packed baseline rather than below it -- the first release for which that is true, reviewed and accepted rather than hidden behind the existing required-artifact exception wording (see packedBudgetPolicy.baselineExceptionReview, which the validator requires before any ceiling at or above the baseline is allowed, and which caps the ceiling at the approved number). Unpacked still lands 14.5% below the baseline. The growth is this release's added surface: every generated artifact grew with it (CEM +0.35 MB, web-types +0.44 MB, editor data +0.23 MB, the authored and generated reference +0.64 MB), plus an eleventh built-in locale (26 shipped files). The file ceiling stays derived, not guessed: 2,500 base artifacts + 288 stable tag aliases x 2 emitted files + the measured entrypoint remainder, plus 7 files of slack so the next scaffolded component does not immediately breach it. Byte ceilings keep their existing 34,000 / 140,000-byte drift headroom, both within the validator's 0.5% cap.

baselineExceptionReview.reason: 16.0.0 is the first release whose required public artifacts exceed the pre-8.0.0 packed baseline. The alternatives were measured and declined: dropping llms-full.txt would have saved 899 KB packed but breaks the llms.txt convention's own link target, and dropping web-types.json would have saved 834 KB by removing JetBrains completions from the installed package. Shipping the full reference and editor data was judged worth 2.1% over the historical baseline. Re-measured at the 16.0.0 release commit: the version bump writes this release's 3,251-line CHANGELOG section into the shipped CHANGELOG.md (+93 KB packed, +270 KB unpacked), which a pre-bump measurement cannot contain, so the ceiling moved from 2.1% to 3.3% over the historical baseline for the same reviewed artifact set.
